transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I almost didn’t want to say it because I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I’ve been having these thoughts like… maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself or anything like that. It’s just been coming into my head, and I thought I should probably talk to someone.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?

I guess… it’s been happening enough lately that it’s what made me come in. I keep catching myself thinking maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I don’t have a plan or anything like that, I promise—it’s more like the thought pops up, and then I feel bad for even having it.
How is your mood been lately?

It’s been… pretty low, I guess. I mean, I’m trying to keep it together, but after that burst of energy wore off, it felt like somebody just pulled the plug on me. I’d sit at the table staring at my coffee and just feel empty… and kind of ashamed, honestly. I don’t know if that makes sense.
How long have you been feeling this low mood?

It’s been… I’d say about three months now, since that crash after the energy wore off. I kept thinking it would pass, so I didn’t want to make too big a deal of it, but yeah… it’s kind of been hanging around that long.
Have you noticed any decrease in interest or pleasure in activities that you normally enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have noticed that. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but the stuff that usually helps me unwind just hasn’t been doing much. Fishing, looking through my vinyl records, tailgating… even checking on my home-brew, it all started feeling more like chores than things I actually wanted to do. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your movement or activity level, such as feeling restless or sluggish?

I’m not really sure… I haven’t noticed anything big like that. Maybe I move a little slower some days, but I don’t know if that’s just being tired or me overthinking it. I wouldn’t want to say yes if it’s not really, you know, a thing.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight lately?

A little, I guess… nothing dramatic, I don’t think. But my jeans have been fitting looser lately. Most days I kind of have to remind myself to eat, and supper just sits there looking like… more trouble than it’s worth. Is that the sort of change you mean?
Have you been feeling guilty about things you've done or haven't done?

Yeah… some. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m sitting around beating myself up all day, but after that burst of energy wore off, it was like somebody pulled the plug on me. I’d just sit at the kitchen table staring into my coffee, feeling kind of empty… and ashamed, I guess. Like I should’ve handled things better somehow. Is that what you mean by guilty?
Have you felt like you're moving slower than usual or had trouble getting started on things?

I don’t think so… not in a way I’d call significant. I mean, some mornings it takes me a bit to get going, but that seems pretty normal, right? I haven’t really noticed myself moving slower than usual or being stuck unable to start things.
Have you been feeling worthless?

Worthless? Um… I don’t know if I’d use that word exactly. I’ve felt kind of down on myself at times, like I’m not doing as well as I should, but “worthless” sounds… pretty harsh. I don’t think I’ve been feeling that, not really. Does that make sense?
Would you say your low mood is present most of the day?

Most of the day… yeah, I guess during that stretch it kind of was. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but after that energy wore off, I felt like somebody had pulled the plug. I’d end up sitting at the table just staring into my coffee, feeling empty and kind of ashamed. So… yes, a lot of the day, I think.
Would you say your low mood is nearly every day?

Yeah… I think it was pretty close to every day, at least during that period. I don’t want to overstate it, but after that burst of energy wore off, it was like the plug got pulled on me. I’d be sitting there staring at my coffee, feeling empty and kind of ashamed. So… yes, nearly every day, I guess.
Have you had any periods where your low mood was significantly worse than others?

Yeah… I think there was a stretch that was worse. After that burst of energy wore off, it just felt like somebody pulled the plug on me. I’d sit at the table staring into my coffee, feeling empty and kind of ashamed. I don’t want to make too big a thing of it, but that part was definitely lower than the rest.
Would you say that even the worse periods of low mood you mentioned still allowed you to function and take care of your daily responsibilities, or were there times when it became very difficult?

I mean… I was still trying, you know? I don’t want to sound like I just gave up. But yeah, there were times it got pretty hard. I fell behind on bills, missed some callbacks and appointments, and I couldn’t really keep a steady job search going even though I needed to.

At home, too, my normal routines got kind of sloppy. I kept telling myself I should be able to just push through it, but… it started feeling like willpower wasn’t enough. Does that make sense?
Did you experience any periods where you were unable to get out of bed or leave the house due to your low mood?

Not completely unable, no… I mean, I usually got up eventually and could leave if I really had to. It was more that I was moving so slow and putting things off, and then stuff started slipping.

Like I fell behind on bills, missed callbacks and appointments, and I couldn’t keep up with looking for work even though I really needed to. Around the house, my usual routines got pretty sloppy too. I kept telling myself, “Just handle it,” but it wasn’t really working. Is that… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say your low mood has interfered with your relationships with family and friends?

I’m not sure it really has, not in a big obvious way. I mean, I may have been a little quieter or not as quick to call people back, but I don’t think I had any major falling-outs or anything like that.

My family probably noticed I wasn’t quite myself, but I tried not to put it on them too much. I guess I’d say it maybe affected things a little, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Have you had any periods where you were completely unable to work or perform daily activities due to your low mood?

Completely unable… I don’t think I’d say completely, no. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was. But it did get to where I wasn’t really functioning the way I should.

I fell behind on bills, missed callbacks and appointments, and I couldn’t keep a steady job search going even though I needed work. And at home, my usual routines got pretty sloppy. I kept telling myself I should just be able to handle it with willpower, but it got obvious that wasn’t really enough. Does that make sense?
Would you say there were times when your low mood made it impossible for you to work or take care of daily responsibilities?

Impossible might be a little strong… I don’t want to overstate it. But there were definitely times it got in the way enough that I wasn’t keeping up.

I fell behind on bills, missed callbacks and appointments, and I just couldn’t keep a steady job search going even though I really needed to. Even around the house, my normal routines got sloppy, and after a while I kind of had to admit I couldn’t just push through it by willpower. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you describe your low mood as mildly bothersome or significantly impacting your life?

I’d probably say… more than mildly bothersome, if I’m being honest. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it did start affecting real-life things.

I fell behind on bills, missed callbacks and appointments, and I couldn’t keep a steady job search going even though I needed to. And at home, my usual routines got pretty sloppy. So, yeah, I guess it was significant enough that I couldn’t just handle it by willpower. Is that a fair way to put it?
Would you say your low mood has caused significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning?

Yeah… I think I’d have to say yes, at least somewhat significantly. I don’t like admitting that, but it did affect things that mattered.

I fell behind on bills, missed callbacks and appointments, and I wasn’t able to keep a steady job search going even though I needed work. And at home, my normal routines got pretty sloppy. It got to the point where I realized I couldn’t just fix it by trying harder, if that makes sense.
